images.title: Height gap of two peaks
images.purpose: Show that the difference in height is found by subtracting: 8848 − 2228 = 6620 m.
images.composition: Two tall bars side by side with wide gap, the extra part of the taller bar highlighted, and one line of working below.
images.exact_structure: Two vertical bars of equal width on one baseline, drawn to scale with 1 unit = 1000 m. Left bar amber #E69F00 about 8.85 units tall for Everest. Right bar teal #0072B2 about 2.23 units tall for Koscuiszko. A dotted grey #6B7280 line runs from the top of the right bar across to the left bar. The part of the left bar above that line is filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 2 bars, 1 highlighted part.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars not drawn to scale, or highlighted part not matching the gap
images.takeaway: How much taller means the difference: subtract the smaller height from the larger.
images.description: Two bars to scale: Everest 8848 m and Koscuiszko 2228 m, with the extra part of the Everest bar highlighted as the 6620 m gap.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the highlighted part and say it is what is left after taking away 2228.

image_decisions.why: The gap is a comparison question, best seen as the extra part of the taller bar.
